''Sonchus libycus'' Spach ex Boiss.
''Sonchus lyratus'' Willd.
''Sonchus squarrosus'' DC. }} '''''Sonchus fruticosus''''', the '''giant sow thistle''', is a species of flowering plant in the tribe [[Cichorieae]] of the family [[Asteraceae]]. It is endemic to the islands of [[Madeira]]. The giant sow thistle is an impressive shrub native to the [[Madeira evergreen forests|Madeiran evergreen forest habitat]] and growing up to {{Convert|4|m|ft|abbr=off}} in height. It is also known as the '''shrubby sonchus''', the '''shrubby sow thistle''',{{cite web |title=Madeira Island Flora |url=https://www.madeirabirds.com/madeiras_flora_madeira_island |website=Madeira Birdwatching News & Trip Reports 🐦 |access-date=17 November 2021 |language=en-gb |date=7 February 2005 |archive-date=17 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117022121/https://www.madeirabirds.com/madeiras_flora_madeira_island |url-status=live }} or the '''Madeiran tree dandelion'''{{cite web |title=Sonchus fruticosus Seeds |url=https://adventurousplants.co.uk/product/sonchus-fruticosus-seeds/ |website=Adventurous Plants |access-date=17 November 2021 |archive-date=17 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117012943/https://adventurousplants.co.uk/product/sonchus-fruticosus-seeds/ |url-status=live }} in English. On Madeira, it is known by the Portuguese vernacular names '''Leituga''',{{cite book |last1=Figueiredo |first1=Albano |title=Calheta : património natural = natural patrimony |date=2008 |publisher=Imprenta da Universidade de Coimbra |location=Coimbra |isbn=9789898074591 |page=98 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SxlEwhGbjPMC&dq=sonchus+fruticosus+leituga&pg=PA47 |access-date=2021-11-26 |archive-date=2022-04-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220418084916/https://books.google.com/books?id=SxlEwhGbjPMC&dq=sonchus+fruticosus+leituga&pg=PA47 |url-status=live }} '''língua de vaca''', and '''serralha da rocha'''.{{cite web |title=Historia Natural de la Macaronesia |url=http://www.macaronesian.org/en/show/leituga-lingua-de-vaca-serralha-da-rocha-sonchus-fruticosus |website=www.macaronesian.org |publisher=Açores-Madeira-Canarias (MAC) |access-date=17 November 2021 |archive-date=17 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117022112/http://www.macaronesian.org/en/show/leituga-lingua-de-vaca-serralha-da-rocha-sonchus-fruticosus |url-status=live }} The term ''leituga'' refers to a broad variety of plants, including prickly lettuce (''[[Lactuca serriola]]'') and cat's ear (''[[Hypochaeris glabra]]'').{{cite web |title=Leituga word origin |url=https://etymologeek.com/por/leituga/86189476 |website=Etymologeek |access-date=17 November 2021 |language=en |archive-date=17 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117022117/https://etymologeek.com/por/leituga/86189476 |url-status=live }} ==Description== [[File:Sonchus fruticosus, Levada das 25 Fontes - Nov 2010.jpg|thumb|right|''Sonchus fruticosus'' growing in context in [[Madeira]]]] ''Sonchus fruticosus'' is a [[perennial plant]], with some descriptions putting the giant sow thistle as [[deciduous plant|deciduous]]. It grows up to {{Convert|6|ft|m|abbr=off}} in height, and some reports putting it at {{Convert|4|m|ft|abbr=off}}. with a woody trunk. Its growing habit is that of a [[subshrub]].{{cite web |title=Sonchus fruticosus {{!}} giant sow thistle Shrubs/RHS Gardening |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/208094/sonchus-fruticosus/details |website=RHS Gardening |publisher=[[Royal Horticultural Society]] |access-date=17 November 2021 |language=en-gb |archive-date=17 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117003710/https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/208094/sonchus-fruticosus/details |url-status=live }} It is a partial evergreen in its native habitat, and loses its leaves during the winter elsewhere. It is found at an elevation of 800 meters to 1200 meters. It takes 2 to 5 years to grow to its peak height, with some report putting this value at 20 to 50 years. Due to its bizarre appearance, resembling that of a giant dandelion, ''S. fruticosus'' is often grown as attractions at gardens and parks, especially in Western European botanical gardens.{{cite web |title=SONCHUS FRUTICOSUS L. f. – mléč / mlieč |url=https://botany.cz/cs/sonchus-fruticosus/ |website=BOTANY.cz |access-date=17 November 2021 |language=cs |archive-date=17 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117022116/https://botany.cz/cs/sonchus-fruticosus/ |url-status=live }} In addition, it is one of the few [[perennial plant]]s and shrubs within the genus ''[[Sonchus]]''. It is part of a group of giant sowthistles found in the [[Macaronesia]]n region within the subgenus ''Dendrosonchus''; such as: ''[[Sonchus acaulis]]'', ''[[Sonchus arboreus]]'', ''[[Sonchus canariensis]]'', ''[[Sonchus congestus]]'', ''[[Sonchus hierrense]]'', and ''[[Sonchus palmensis]]''.{{cite web |title=Sonchus (Giant Sowthistle) --- Rareplants.eu |url=http://www.rareplants.de/shop/prodtype.asp?CAT_ID=255 |website=www.rareplants.de |access-date=17 November 2021 |archive-date=17 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117012701/http://www.rareplants.de/shop/prodtype.asp?CAT_ID=255 |url-status=live }} The giant sow thistle has glossy toothed green leaves, with [[denticulate leaf|denticulate margin]], sinuate, and long, growing to a length of {{Convert|50|cm|ft|abbr=off}} and arranged in a [[rosette (botany)|rosette]]. The rosette grows to a width of {{Convert|0.5|m|ft|abbr=off}} to {{Convert|1|m|ft|abbr=off}}. It flowers during the summer, during the months of June, July, and August, with yellow flowers that resemble [[dandelions]]. The flowers are attractive to bees, butterflies, and birds. The seeds are [[wind dispersal|wind dispersed]]. Sonchus fruticosus seedlings II, by Omar Hoftun.jpg|''Sonchus fruticosus'' seedlings Madeira - Dandelion Tree - Sonchus fruticosus (24540878402).jpg|Detail of leaves Sonchus fruticosus - Levada das 25 Fontes - 2.jpg|Growing in context at [[Levada das 25 Fontes]] Sonchusfruticosus.jpg|Infructescence ===Care=== The giant sow thistle requires direct sunlight or partial shade. It requires regular or little watering, but prefers moist soil. The giant sow thistle is drought tolerant.{{cite web |last1=Whitinger |first1=Dave |title=PlantFiles: Giant Sow Thistle |url=https://davesgarden.com/guides/pf/go/194720/#b |website=[[Dave's Garden]] |access-date=17 November 2021 |language=en |archive-date=17 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117010815/https://davesgarden.com/guides/pf/go/194720/#b |url-status=live }} It generally requires average, well drained soil, and free-draining, loam-based compost. The recommended [[pH]] is between 5.5 and 8.5. It prefers chalky, loamy, or sandy soil. It prefers a garden aspect facing south, east, or west. Its [[Hardiness_zone#Britain_and_Ireland|UK hardiness zone]] is H3 (tender in frost) and H1 (indoor heated), its [[Hardiness_zone#United_States_hardiness_zones_(USDA_scale)|USDA hardiness zone]] is 9a, 9b, 10a, 10b, and 11. It is an outdoors plant during the summer, and is recommended to be overwintered indoors. If planted outdoors, the plant can survive a frost, with the top growth being shed while the roots survive. However, roots cannot survive freezing. It is generally pest and disease free. However vagrant populations of the aphid ''[[Uroleucon mierae]]'' and the leafhopper ''[[Empoasca fabalis]]'' are known to feed on the flowers and leaves respectively.{{cite web |title=Sonchus fruticosus – Plant Parasites of Europe |url=https://bladmineerders.nl/host-plants/plantae/spermatopsida/angiosperma/eudicots/superasterids/asterids/campanulids/asterales/asteraceae/cichoroideae/cichorieae/hyoseridinae/sonchus/sonchus-fruticosus/ |website=Plant Parasites of Europe |access-date=17 November 2021 |archive-date=8 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210508065210/https://bladmineerders.nl/host-plants/plantae/spermatopsida/angiosperma/eudicots/superasterids/asterids/campanulids/asterales/asteraceae/cichoroideae/cichorieae/hyoseridinae/sonchus/sonchus-fruticosus/ |url-status=live }} The giant sow thistle does not require pruning, with leaves being trimmed off if necessary. To propagate seeds, it is recommended to sow during the spring or summer, during the months of April and May, with a minimum outdoor temperature of {{Convert|25|C|F|abbr=off}}. If propagating during winter, sow in vented containers, coldframe, or an unheated greenhouse. It is recommended to sow indoors or directly before the last frost. To collect the seeds, bag the seedheads to capture the ripe seeds. The plant can self-sow, with [[Deadheading (flowers)|deadheading]] recommended if one does not want [[volunteer (botany)|volunteer seedling]]s. It can be propagated by root cuttings, seeds,{{cite web |title=Sonchus fruticosus Giant sow thistle Phyllocephalum frutescens Care Plant Varieties & Pruning Advice |url=https://www.shootgardening.co.uk/plant/sonchus-fruticosus |website=Shoot Gardening |publisher=Shoot Limited |access-date=17 November 2021 |language=en |archive-date=17 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117010809/https://www.shootgardening.co.uk/plant/sonchus-fruticosus |url-status=live }} herbaceous stem cuttings, softwood cuttings, and by [[air layering]]. ==Distribution== The giant sow thistle is found on the islands of [[Madeira]].{{cite web |title=Sonchus fruticosus L.f. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:250146-1 |website=[[Plants of the World Online]] |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|Kew Science]] |access-date=17 November 2021 |language=en |archive-date=23 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211023180108/http://www.plantsoftheworldonline.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:250146-1 |url-status=live }}{{cite web |title=Sonchus fruticosus, Sow-thistle in GardenTags plant encyclopedia |url=https://www.gardentags.com/plant-encyclopedia/sonchus-fruticosus/16259 |website=GardenTags |access-date=17 November 2021 |archive-date=17 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117011033/https://www.gardentags.com/plant-encyclopedia/sonchus-fruticosus/16259 |url-status=live }} Where it grows within the [[Laurel_forest#Laurel_forest_ecoregions_of_Macaronesia|Northern laurisilva cloud forest]] habitat within [[Madeira evergreen forests|Madeira]], at an elevation of 800-1200 meters. There have been reports of giant sow thistles on the island of [[Porto Santo Island|Porto Santo]], where it is rare. There are additional, albeit unreliable, records of ''S. fruticosus'' being found on the [[Canary Islands]].{{cite web |title=Sonchus fruticosus {{!}} plant lust |url=https://plantlust.com/plants/13078/sonchus-fruticosus/ |website=Plant Lust |publisher=Plant Lust, LLC |access-date=17 November 2021 |language=en |archive-date=17 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117003711/https://plantlust.com/plants/13078/sonchus-fruticosus/ |url-status=live }} However it is doubtful that the plant is native to the Canary Islands. ==See also== *[[Island endemic|Island endemism]] *[[Island gigantism]] ==External links== *[http://www.africanplants.senckenberg.de/root/index.php?page_id=78&id=9331 African Plants repository of regional database entries regarding ''Sonchus fruticosus''] ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q10373280}} [[Category:Sonchus|fruticosus]] [[Category:Plants described in 1782]] [[Category:Taxa named by Carl Linnaeus the Younger]] [[Category:Endemic flora of Madeira]]
